newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks likely to be stuck in narrow range.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks likely to be stuck in narrow range.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to be stuck in a narrow range on Monday, lacking concrete trading factors, brokers said. They added that with the yen near 115 to the dollar following the Group of Seven (G7) summit, investors may be interested in export-oriented issues.
On Friday, the Nikkei average ended 122.31 points or 0.60 percent lower at 20,385.54. Its September futures rose 30 to 20,470.
"A strong statement on Japan's increasing trade surplus was not made at the G7 summit meeting, which was pretty much as expected," a general manager at a second-tier brokerage said.

Although the Denver summit -- which had been forcing investors onto the sidelines due to anxieties over currencies -- was now over, brokers said that the Bank of Japan's "tankan" survey on business sentiment was still hanging over the market.
The tankan will be released on Wednesday.
"Signs of recovery in consumer spending after the consumption tax was raised in April will help the Nikkei average post gains, if they start appearing," one broker said.
Wall Street's record close on Friday and a rise in the Nikkei 225 futures in Chicago, could provide support as well, brokers said.
"The Nikkei average started slipping past the 20,500 level last week and the market is keen to see if that level is going to be the floor or the ceiling," a broker at a second-tier brokerage said.

"Global issues such as Sony Corp and Toyota Motor Corp are still pretty much in a correction phase and smaller shares with good earnings prospects are being bought," a "Big Four" broker said. "But shares such as Fujitsu do not have enough strength to pull the whole market higher."
Japan Tobacco Inc (JT) slipped on news that the U.S. tobacco industry, health advocates and 40 states suing the industry had reached a $368.5 billion landmark settlement on Friday.
Shares of JT fell 26,000 yen to stand at 911,000.
"There is speculation that such a settlement will hasten anti-smoking moves even in Japan, which would be damaging to JT's business," a trader at a foreign brokerage said.
"But trade in the shares is extremely thin, exaggerating the fall, and the weakness will probably be temporary."
The largest percentage gainer on the first section was Taka-Q Co Ltd, which rose 25 yen or 8.04 percent to reach 336.
The shares of the retailer were inspired by news that it was planning to form a joint venture with a Bermuda-based holding company of Esprit Holdings Ltd.

By sector, rubber, automobiles, pulp/paper, precision instruments and fisheries were at the top of the list of gainers. The retreaters were headed by warehouses, pharmaceuticals, credit/lease, securities and air transport.
The TOPIX added 0.66 point or 0.04 percent to finish the morning at 1,530.90. The Nikkei 300 added 0.39 point or 0.13 percent to reach 296.24.
